issue.title: changed pls_.py to properly scale data, modified documents
issue.body:
1.  In many instances of the variable `scale` setting was ignored.  Data was always centered, and always scaled.  The data is now scaled appropriately when `scale=True` is set, and not scaled when it's `False`
2. The return from the `predict()` function was always de-centered, but never de-scaled, so that we got:
   `Ypred = Ypred + self.y_mean_`  for all cases
   instead of:
   `Ypred = (Ypred * self.y_std_) + self.y_mean_` when `scale=True`
3. In the nipals algorithm, either C and Q matrices are used for deflation modes (regression or canonical).  This is now implemented.  The #FIXME note is now not necessary, as `coef_` is calculated differently depending on those two cases.  The calculated `coef_` was also scaled unnecesarily by standard deviations of X and Y: this is now commented out.  Only matrices W and C are scaled by their norms in the inner loop.  The outer loop scales P, Q, and C (canonical and regression) matrices by `T.T*T` or `U.T*U`
4. Some documentation was changed to reflect code modifications.  Also, instructions to use `sklearn.preprocessing.scale` are included, as that could be a useful step for most users.
5. It should be noted that the example included in the comment sections now gives better predictions of Y.
6. if X and Y are scaled using `sklearn.preprocessing.scale` (or column mean centered and column variance scaled), the pls_ functions all return the SAME results when `scale=True` and  `scale=False` this was not the case in the previous version of the code

body:
I can reproduce the test failure on an Ubuntu 14.04 box. A snippet that reproduces the problem:

```
conda create -y -n tmp python=3.5 numpy scipy nose cython
source activate tmp
make clean && make in && nosetests sklearn/cross_decomposition/tests/test_pls.py -m test_scale
```

The failure happens with both python 2.7 and 3.5. Not sure why we are not seeing it on Travis. Note I wasn't able to reproduce the failure on my laptop running Ubuntu 15.10. This seems slightly weird, so I'll double-check tonight that I didn't do anything stupid.

> Note I wasn't able to reproduce the failure on my laptop running Ubuntu 15.10. This seems slightly weird, so I'll double-check tonight that I didn't do anything stupid.

Double-checked and indeed the test pass on my Ubuntu 15.10 laptop, interesting !
Indeed, this is probably because of latest MKL used for latest numpy / scipy with conda. I tried to fix the gfortran issue on travis master in #6494 and I triggered this issue...

I get `pls_.py:314: UserWarning: X scores are null at iteration 1
  warnings.warn('X scores are null at iteration %s' % k)
` when using scaling.
took me a bit to find out that the omnipotent part is failing, not the scaling part.

There is an 1e-17 difference on X between before and after scaling. That propagates to an 1e-17 difference in `Y_k` in the first iteration.
The one were scaling was applied twice has

```
array([[ 0.        , -0.0249032 ],
       [ 0.        ,  0.05861063],
       [ 0.        , -0.06155424],
       [ 0.        ,  0.02784681]])
```

The other one has some 1e-16 entries in the first column. So now Y_k is rank 1 and the solver doesn't do anything in the next iteration.

The test says

```
    # Test with X2, T2 s.t. clf.x_score[:, 1] == 0, clf.y_score[:, 1] == 0
    # This test robustness of algorithm when dealing with value close to 0
```

@arthurmensch you wrote this. can you explain?
